pr_body:
In https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/34633#issuecomment-746681771 a product bug in regards of logging was found.
This didn't show up in tests, as it was disabled for Windows https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/911b1d395ef4e59c63048003d676e295414c8d15/src/libraries/System.Net.NameResolution/tests/FunctionalTests/LoggingTest.cs#L66 and prior #34633 Unix was async-over-sync, so didn't touch this test in the same way is it does now.

On local testing I couldn't spot any unrealiable behavior, per https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/34633#discussion_r544521828 we should give this a try to see what happens.

---

Edit: Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/47104

This is the timing issue outlined in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/47034#discussion_r558374191, unfortunately it's bites us (me) here.

But that will be fixed with https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/47034, as the [latest commit there](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/47034/commits/b723ccd03e2c27b45d24e757ddcf9433a62966a8) has a robust handling for the events.
@gfoidl great! Can you please update the PR description that it fixes this issue?

review_comments:
I'm skeptical any time I see a construct like:
```C#
await Task.Delay(100).ConfigureAwait(false);
```
used for synchronization.  But if it's not been failing on Unix, I'm not sure why it'd be any more likely to fail on Windows.
Yep, that's not ideal. Is for the event source a better way to "wait" until the log is written?
I'm wondering if we could emit some other known event and wait for that to arrive. And assume the events are processed in sequence. @MihaZupan  would probably know how the events are processed.

We should use something like [`WaitForEventAsync`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a3b37a289b00c748eb92bd4eb4dc78146bd72176/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/tests/FunctionalTests/TelemetryTest.cs#L418) we used in Sockets telemetry across all such tests.
